newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court rejects passive smoking death case.
newsitem.headline: French court rejects passive smoking death case.

text.p: A Paris court rejected on Wednesday a claim by the family of a non-smoker who died of lung cancer for compensation from her former employer for failing to enforce no-smoking laws at work.

In a lawsuit unprecedented in France, the court threw out a claim for 50,000 francs ($10,000) by the family of Leila Ozeir, saying there was insufficient proof to link her fatal illness to passive smoking at her job in the Banque Francaise de l'Orient.
Even so, the court agreed that the bank failed to comply with the so-called Evin laws of 1991 that limit smoking in workplaces.
It also agreed that passive smoking created risks of cancer.
A ruling in favour of the family could have opened the gates to a flood of similar claims in France.
"Tobacco companies are very powerful. In America it would be different. In France, the Evin law is not well implemented," said Roze Ozeir, Leila's sister.
